results.title: Advisory locks in PostgreSQL
results.snippet: Application-defined locks identified by a 64-bit key, held per session or per transaction.
results.content: pg_advisory_lock(key) blocks until the lock is free; pg_try_advisory_lock returns at once. Session-level locks survive transactions and must be released; transaction-level locks (pg_advisory_xact_lock) end with the transaction. They don't lock rows: they are for coordinating application work.

results.title: Row locks vs advisory locks
results.snippet: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks real rows; advisory locks lock an idea.
results.content: Prefer row locks when the thing you protect is a row: they compose with your data. Advisory locks fit leader election and one-at-a-time jobs. Neither replaces fencing tokens when a lock holder can pause and wake up after its lock was taken over.
